What comes up in Killara

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table is what the work usually involves here rather than a statement about any particular property.

Demolition around protected trees

The Killara job in a sentence: a generous block, a substantial house and plantings that set the method.

How it is handled
Protection zones established first, the demolition sequenced around them, and material moved by hand where plant cannot go.
What does it
Midi excavator outside the protection zone, hand work close in.

Dig into a falling block

Where the ground changes partway down and the method has to change with it.

How it is handled
Reassessed as the dig goes down, with rock hammered and priced by the cubic metre at an agreed rate rather than guessed at.
What does it
Large excavator with a toothed bucket and a hydraulic hammer.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Killara

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Large established blocks Deep lots with substantial houses and generous setbacks.
  • Significant trees The defining constraint. Tree approval is routinely the longest item on a clearing programme here.
  • Blocks falling into gullies Where a dig can start in shale derived clay and finish in sandstone.
  • Heritage and conservation controls Common through the leafier streets, and a planning matter to settle before a scope is written.

Killara blocks have room, but the plantings decide where plant can stand and how material leaves. A protected tree keeps its root zone clear of machines and stockpiles, which frequently means a smaller machine working for longer and material moved by hand close in.

Killara questions

What people ask before we start

How long does tree approval take?
It depends entirely on the council and the tree, and it is not something a contractor can shortcut. It is worth starting well before the demolition or clearing is programmed, because it is routinely the longest item.
Will the dig hit rock?
It can, particularly where the block falls away. A geotechnical report narrows the range a long way; without one, rock is priced by the cubic metre at a rate agreed before the dig starts.
What about the trees?
They are frequently the longest item. Tree removal depends on approval, and in Killara and Lindfield particularly the plantings are significant enough that the approval process should start well before the work is programmed.
Who signs off that the asbestos is gone?
An independent licensed assessor, not the removalist and not us. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, the removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the clearance is arranged as part of the same job.
